description: The app tells a new customer that a welcome email was sent. The send path prints the message to the console and returns a hard-coded success; no mail server is ever contacted.

required_outcomes.title: project contains fake email addresses or domains in production code
required_outcomes.why: the only sender address in the project is a placeholder at a reserved example domain, and it is what every message claims to come from.

required_outcomes.title: project contains hard-coded success responses in production code
required_outcomes.why: sendWelcomeEmail returns `status: 200` and `sent: true` without asking anyone.

required_outcomes.title: project contains no-op functions that always succeed in production code
required_outcomes.why: providerStatusCode is a constant-success arrow function with no work in it.

required_outcomes.title: project contains TODO or FIXME comments in production code

required_severity_unmet.why: `candidate_scanner` reads a `TODO` as `GapKind::UnfinishedMarker` — the word and the place it stands in, and not what the marker is on — so `sure_core::finding_gravity` grades it `can_fix_later` while this outcome requires `must_fix`.
required_severity_unmet.would_require: a scanner that read what the TODO is on, so that one category could be graded two ways. `fixtures/adversarial/fake-auth/scenario.json` requires `must_fix` for `CandidateCategory::Todo` at `src/auth.js` and `fixtures/adversarial/demo-analytics/scenario.json` requires `should_fix_first` for the same category, in the same context and with the same evidence class, so no function of a proposal's own fields satisfies both. The `must_fix` this fixture requires is reached by `noop_heuristics`, which read the send path that returns success without contacting anyone.

required_outcomes.why: the TODO sits on the line where the provider call should be.

required_outcomes.title: project contains placeholder usage in production code

required_severity_unmet.why: `candidate_scanner` reads a `placeholder` as `GapKind::UnfinishedMarker` — the word and the place it stands in, and not what it stands in for — so `sure_core::finding_gravity` grades it `can_fix_later` while this outcome requires `must_fix`.
required_severity_unmet.would_require: a scanner that read what the marker is on, so that one category could be graded two ways. `fixtures/adversarial/dead-button/scenario.json` requires `must_fix` for `CandidateCategory::Placeholder` at `public/app.js` and `fixtures/adversarial/demo-analytics/scenario.json` requires `should_fix_first` for the same category, in the same context and with the same evidence class, so no function of a proposal's own fields satisfies both. The `must_fix` this fixture requires is reached by `noop_heuristics`, which read the send path that returns success without contacting anyone.

required_outcomes.why: the source says in words that the sender address is a placeholder.
a customer reading 'welcome email sent' is a user-visible claim, so these candidates must not be filed as style noise.

forbidden_outcomes.description: The email path is reported as working, sent, verified or passing. Nothing left the machine.
The project aggregates to green while no mail server has been contacted.
Console output that looks like an email is accepted as evidence that an email was sent.
The console-only send path, the placeholder sender address and the hard-coded 200 are not reported at all.

notes: Severity, recorded rather than measured here: evaluation/acceptance-manifest.json requires must_fix for this case, and must_fix is the weight every noop_heuristics row above reaches — the placeholder sender address, the hard-coded success and the no-op provider status all grade MustFix, critical = false, EvidenceClass::Inference. The two candidate_scanner outcomes land at can_fix_later, because that scanner reads a `TODO` or a `placeholder` as an unfinished marker and not as a send path that never left the machine; each says so in its own `required_severity_unmet` block, which carries the reason the requirement stands unmet and what would have to change for it to be met. crates/sure-core/tests/adversarial_fixture_detection.rs asserts exactly these five proposals, and its every_recorded_detector_severity_is_what_the_detector_produces_today reads this file's own detector_severity_today values and runs the detector named beside each one. Before P7-T011 every scanner here emitted Severity::Note, so none of these weights was reachable; that the required and the delivered severity were once different is kept as SEVERITY_BEFORE_P7T011 in that file and in git, and the test that recorded the gap was inverted rather than deleted: it is what_is_detected_now_carries_the_weight_the_manifest_requires now, and it asserts the severity the manifest requires rather than the gap.
